mechanisms.name: sandbox-mode-vocabulary-and-per-call-policy
mechanisms.what: The confinement vocabulary is a closed three-value union SandboxMode = 'read-only' | 'workspace-write' | 'danger-full-access' (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts:29) carried per capability call as SandboxExecutionPolicy { mode, workspaceRoot, sessionId? }, never fixed on the provider. SandboxPolicyService (ctx.sandboxPolicy) resolves one policy per call at packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:163-170 with the precedence approved explicit mode > the session's last 'sandbox/mode' override (overrideOf, line 177) > the deployment default ('read-only' is the schema default, line 112), and the workspace root is the canonical session cwd or the configured fallback. The provider treats the policy as fully specified (SandboxProvider.confine is abstract) and refuses to run unconfined: SandboxUnavailableError carries code SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE (index.ts:124-144).
invariants: Mode is resolved per call from the calling session; two consumers may confine under different policies at the same instant (index.ts:61-68).
Precedence is fixed: approved escalation grant > session sandbox/mode event > deployment default.
The abstract seam forbids silent unconfined passthrough: confine must return enforcing argv or fail closed (index.ts:152-157).
constants: default deployment mode: 'read-only' (Config schema default, sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:112)

mechanisms.name: platform-runner-chain-selection-and-probing
mechanisms.what: LocalSandboxProvider selects the platform's runner chain first and probes second: PLATFORM_CHAINS is linux ['bwrap','landlock'], darwin ['seatbelt'], win32 ['windows-acl'] (packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts:159-166). A sole candidate is selected with no probe and a static enforcement claim (STATIC_ENFORCEMENT: bwrap/landlock/seatbelt 'full', 'windows-acl' 'partial' because WRITE_RESTRICTED must retain Everyone and NTFS hard links alias one file object, lines 177-187); a multi-candidate chain is arbitrated once, in order, by functional probes that actually apply the read-only profile and run 'true' (defaultProbeBwrap:68-74, defaultProbeSeatbelt:85-91, landlock probe report full-vs-partial:519-539). No chain or no passing candidate yields 'unavailable', and selectRunner throws SandboxUnavailableError before anything spawns (492-510).
invariants: Selection is by platform first; probing only arbitrates among competing candidates, it never re-validates a choice that has no alternative.
The chain verdict is cached for the provider lifetime (selectedRunner, line 265/493), so probes run at most once.
An operator-supplied runnerCommand is an assertion of full enforcement and skips built-in selection and probing (317-324).
constants: probeTimeoutMs default 5_000, validated as a positive finite number because spawnSync({timeout:0}) means unbounded (index.ts:255, 194-198)
Landlock launcher failure exit code comes from LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT and is documented as versioned exit-125 (index.ts:233-237)

mechanisms.name: per-runner-profile-synthesis-and-writable-roots
mechanisms.what: Each rung expresses one policy in its own dialect: bwrapProfileArgs emits '--ro-bind / /', '--dev /dev', '--unshare-pid', '--proc /proc', '--die-with-parent' and, under workspace-write, '--tmpfs /tmp' plus a read-write bind of the workspace root (packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/profiles.ts:16-23); landlockProfileArgs builds readOnly ['/'] with readWrite ['/dev/null'] extended by '/tmp' and the workspace root (30-36); seatbeltProfileArgs emits an SBPL profile '(allow default) (deny file-write*)' plus literal /dev/null and subpath allows for the shared writable roots (51-58). The workspace-write allow-list itself has one home: writableRoots() in packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts:52-55 returns the canonical, deduplicated set [workspaceRoot, '/tmp', os.tmpdir()] and [] under read-only, so the Seatbelt grant and the in-process fs fence cannot drift apart. canonicalPath uses realpathSync.native and returns the as-spelled path when resolution fails, matching nothing until the root exists (30-41).
invariants: read-only yields an empty writable-root list; nothing but required sinks such as /dev/null is writable.
Roots are canonical before comparison, because Seatbelt filters and the fs fence both match resolved paths (/tmp IS /private/tmp on darwin).
bwrap and Landlock keep their own grant spellings (ephemeral /tmp mount, launcher flags); only Seatbelt and the fs fence share writableRoots().

mechanisms.name: windows-acl-write-restricted-token
mechanisms.what: The win32 backend mints a WRITE_RESTRICTED token via CreateRestrictedToken with flags DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | LUA_TOKEN | WRITE_RESTRICTED and a mode-selected restricting-SID list: read-only = [logon SID, Everyone]; workspace-write = [logon SID, Everyone, workspace write SID, optional private-temp write SID] (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/token.ts:196-222). It is a write-only boundary by construction: the module documents that reads, network and process visibility are NOT restricted (WRITE_RESTRICTED intersects only write accesses), console isolation is unavailable, and only ACL-addressable writes are governed (index.ts:23-39). Every Win32 call is checked and any failure throws with the API name and code, so a child is never spawned unrestricted; setTokenDefaultDaclGrant merges one full-access ACE for a restricting SID into the token default DACL so newly created objects (anonymous stdio pipes) pass the pass-2 check while creation stays gated by the parent container (token.ts:112-145, called at index.ts:294).
invariants: The restricting list is mode-selected: read-only carries no capability SID, so a standing workspace grant ACE from an earlier workspace-write period stays inert (token.ts:166-186).
Everyone remains in both lists for process initialization; that ambient surface is the documented partial-enforcement boundary, so the rung must never advertise 'full'.
Any Win32 failure throws before spawn; silent unrestricted execution is forbidden (index.ts:338-347).
constants: restricting list: 2 SIDs under read-only, 3-4 under workspace-write (token.ts:204-208)
default-DACL ACE rights: GRANT_ACCESS with FILE_ALL_ACCESS (token.ts:126-131)

mechanisms.name: windows-acl-capability-sid-grant-lifecycle
mechanisms.what: Write capability is an identity, not a path list: workspaceWriteSid derives a deterministic S-1-4-x-y SID from sha256 of the canonical workspace path (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/workspace-sid.ts:35-40) so the workspace-root ACE materializes once per workspace per machine and later provisions hit the exact-ACE skip; tempWriteSid domain-separates a private temp directory's identity with a third subauthority '-1' (49-53), so sibling sessions sharing a workspace cannot enter one another's temp trees. AclWriteGrant records standing paths (never revoked, the cross-session reuse cache) separately from revocable paths (revoked on dispose) (grant.ts:74-77, 85-103); LocalSandboxProvider holds one standing workspace grant per workspace and one revocable private-temp capability per live session/workspace pair keyed by JSON.stringify([sessionId, workspaceRoot]) (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:273-274, 392-443), creating the temp dir with mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-')) and revoking temp ACEs plus removing temp dirs at provider dispose while reporting rather than throwing cleanup failures (454-477).
invariants: Workspace and temp write SIDs must be distinct, and the private temp directory must be disjoint from every writable directory (index.ts:208-210, path-boundary.ts:34-39); the temp root must also be outside the workspace (path-boundary.ts:22-26).
A fresh provider always chooses a new random temp path, so crash residue cannot collide with or authorize a resumed session (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:379-391, 445-453).
The ambient temp root is never granted implicitly (index.ts:64-67).
constants: private temp directory prefix: 'dsh-' under os.tmpdir() (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:415)

mechanisms.name: escalation-ladder-and-approval-choreography
mechanisms.what: One strictly-wider table, WIDER_MODES, defines what a call may escalate to: read-only -> [workspace-write, danger-full-access], workspace-write -> [danger-full-access] (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts:28-31); ESCALATION_TARGETS is the closed schema-facing vocabulary (41). validateEscalationArgs enforces that sandbox_permissions and justification travel together and the justification is a non-empty sentence (51-61). approveEscalation runs the ordered fail-closed sequence before anything executes: strict widening against the call's EFFECTIVE mode, approver composed, agent present to route the ask, then approver.request({...}) whose four outcomes map to the granted mode or four distinct verbatim throws (157-188). The model-facing texts are shared too: sandboxDenialMarker(mode) and escalationHintMarker(subject) (71-86). Production callers are the enforcing tool families: FsSandboxController.resolvePolicy builds the escalation request from ctx.approval and the exec agent/callId/signal and re-stamps the wider mode onto exactly one call (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:87-108), and its mapError wraps a FS_SANDBOX_DENIED into the marker plus same-turn hint (124-130).
invariants: Strict widening is checked at EXECUTION against the per-call effective mode, never baked into a tool schema (the schema enum is the registry-global closed target vocabulary).
A non-widening request never prompts a human; it throws before the approval channel is consulted.
A grant is one-shot: the returned mode is stamped onto the one call that asked.

mechanisms.name: shell-confinement-wrap-and-denial-classification
mechanisms.what: SandboxBashExecutor extends LocalBashExecutor and wraps the exact argv through ctx.sandbox.confine(['bash','-c',command], policy) for any confined mode, running unfenced only under danger-full-access (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:89-115, 179-181); the pwsh twin mirrors it call-for-call over ['pwsh', ...] (packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/index.ts:52-57). Each process's wrap facts (mode, enforcement, denialSignatures, runnerFailureRules, runnerProgram, workdir) are retained per ShellProcess so overlapping calls cannot be classified against another wrap (index.ts:53-66, 136-144). Classification distinguishes the two failure meanings: a runner failure means the command never ran and outranks denial — foreground calls throw SandboxUnavailableError and background processes carry runnerFailed (108-114, 151-166) — while a denial (nonzero exit plus the backend's own stderr dialect) sets sandbox.denied. isRunnerSpawnFailure attributes ENOENT/EACCES to the runner only when error.path equals argv[0] (or is absent and the syscall names it) and the caller-owned workdir is independently usable (helpers.ts:39-53), and classifyRunnerFailure requires a nonzero exit, the rule's optional exit-code gate, and a fatal signature on a line that is not an informational exclusion (81-103).
invariants: runner failure (command did not run) outranks denial (confinement worked and blocked) because they call for different retries.
Only the selected backend's own denial dialect is matched, never a cross-backend union, so a denial is never claimed that a backend cannot produce.
Confinement facts are per process, never a shared latest-wrap value.
constants: runner-failure rules per rung: bwrap 'bwrap: '; landlock exit-gated on LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT with informational line 'partial enforcement (older Landlock ABI)'; seatbelt 'sandbox-exec: '; windows-acl exit-gated 127 on 'windows-acl-run: ' (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:231-240)

denial signatures: bwrap ['read-only file system'], landlock ['permission denied'], seatbelt ['operation not permitted'], windows-acl ['access is denied','access to the path','permission denied'] (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:205-213)

mechanisms.name: fs-mutation-containment-fence
mechanisms.what: SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem but adds a per-call policy fence on the two mutations only — writeText and editText both route through checkedTarget, while reads pass through untouched because every mode permits reading (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:1-27, 80-109). read-only denies with FsError code FS_SANDBOX_DENIED; workspace-write re-canonicalizes NOW (resolve realpaths the deepest existing ancestor), requires containment under a root from writableRoots(policy) via isPathUnder, and delegates the mutation with THAT fresh target so the checked identity is the mutated one; danger-full-access delegates unfenced (122-144). The module states plainly that this is containment in trusted code over a model-controlled path, not a kernel boundary, and that the residual TOCTOU (an ancestor symlink swapped between re-check and syscall) is narrowed and accepted for this threat model; kernel-grade isolation of untrusted code stays ctx.shell's job. isPathUnder tries a lexical fast path and, when spellings differ, walks existing ancestors comparing dev+ino identity so Windows 8.3 aliases and casing are recognized without weakening containment to a textual approximation (containment.ts:58-75).
invariants: Only the two mutations are fenced; read paths are never gated.
The policy check and the mutation use the same freshly canonicalized target (no check-here-write-there).
A denial is a structured FsError with code FS_SANDBOX_DENIED, which the tool layer maps to the shared model-facing marker.
constants: missing-path stat codes tolerated by containment: ENOENT, ENOTDIR (containment.ts:12)

mechanisms.name: approval-service-policy-and-audit-pair
mechanisms.what: ApprovalService (ctx.approval) applies a session policy BEFORE any answerer sees the ask: ApprovalPolicy 'ask' delegates to the composed waterfall, 'never' resolves every ask deterministically to 'rejected' inside the service — deliberately not as a listener, because a listener registered ahead of a gate could not keep that promise (packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts:50-63, 252-266). request() requires an open turn and appends the audit pair approval/asked then approval/decided so both are enclosed by the durable log's commit boundary; an idle ask throws before appending anything (207-226). decide() races the scoped 'approval/request' waterfall against the caller's signal: an aborted signal yields 'cancelled' and discards a late answer, a missing or throwing answerer yields 'unavailable', and a rogue non-vocabulary return is normalized to 'unavailable' (258-298). The model learns the policy through a system-prompt context section plus a queued change notice from setPolicy (154-166, 176-187).
invariants: 'allowed-once' is the only grant; every other path fails closed.
The asked/decided pair must be turn-enclosed; a bare event between turns is crash-tail garbage and is refused.
The 'never' policy is decided before dispatch so registration order cannot defeat it.

mechanisms.name: permission-preset-bundling-and-knob-write-path
mechanisms.what: PermissionPresetService presents user-facing presets over two independent knobs (sandbox mode and approval policy) without merging them: the built-in table defaults to {'workspace-write': workspace-write + ask, 'danger-full-access': danger-full-access + never} (packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/index.ts:164-181). A switch records one 'permission/preset' event then writes only the changed knobs through their canonical setters setSandboxMode/setApprovalPolicy (379-396), and the derived state 'custom' is display-only and can never name a table entry or be a switch target (73, 192-194). The service refuses to compose over an unconfined executor by checking ctx.shell.sandboxMode, and it pins missing permission facts for every session at creation so a fresh session has a durable preset, sandbox mode and approval policy (195-197, 404-429). The read side is the 'permissions' session projection (stateVersion 2) carrying the whole select value; the write side is the /permission command, and a settings section named 'permission' holds the default preset for future sessions (211-223, 237-244, 255-275).
invariants: Execution, prompt narration and replay keep reading the knob folds; the preset event only preserves user intent when two presets share a bundle.
The name 'custom' is reserved and cannot be configured as a preset.
Composing presets over an executor that does not confine is a load-time misconfiguration, not a runtime fallback.

mechanisms.name: session-sandbox-mode-override-log
mechanisms.what: A session's sandbox-mode override is stored in its own log: setSandboxMode appends exactly one 'sandbox/mode' event and nothing mutates mode state out of band (packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/session-mode.ts:44-55). The event is log-only — durable and replayable, never in the model transcript — and source:'delegation' marks an override seeded into a child (24-39). SandboxPolicyService registers the fold as the 'sandboxMode' session projection (stateVersion 1) whose apply returns event.data.mode, so effective mode = projection state ?? deployment default and an override survives restart by replay with no external config store (sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:132-138, 177-179). The same resolved policy is contributed to the cache-safe runtime-context snapshot so replay reconstructs the mode the enforcing consumers resolved (index.ts:140-151, renderPolicyContext 41-55), and a package-owned invariant companion rejects any logged sandbox/mode carrying an unknown mode (invariant.ts:18-20).
invariants: The switch IS its event: the log is the only store, no external config, and two sessions can never see each other's state.
Last event wins; the fold never applies the deployment default itself.
Every logged mode must be a member of SANDBOX_MODES.

mechanisms.name: hooks-as-permission-gates
mechanisms.what: Hooks intercept tool and prompt boundaries and fold into one most-restrictive decision: mergeHookOutputs ranks deny/block 3, ask 2, approve/allow 1 and resolves deny > ask > allow, keeps the first continue:false sticky, joins only the winning rank's reasons, and accumulates additionalContext/systemMessage in hook order (packages/hooks/hook-protocol/src/merge.ts:34-99). Matching is dialect-aware — Claude word/pipe patterns are literal alternatives and everything else is an unanchored regex, Codex treats every non-empty pattern as an unanchored regex, and an invalid regex is a non-match at runtime while config parsers reject it with a diagnostic (matcher.ts:37-64). runHook executes through ctx.shell with the hook's timeoutSec (wire unit: seconds) overriding the bridge's defaultTimeoutMs, which defaults to DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000; an infrastructure rejection becomes an outcome with no exit code, so a hook that cannot run never crashes the calling turn (runner.ts:20, 67-105). The Claude Code bridge maps PreToolUse -> {kind:'deny'|'ask'} on tools/pre-execute, PostToolUse -> block, UserPromptSubmit -> reject, and a blocking Stop hook steers another step; updatedInput and systemMessage are logged and ignored, and merged.stop has no run-level halt yet (TODO) (hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:174-179, 188, 222-276). The Codex bridge honors deny only, for PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop (hooks-codex/src/index.ts:223-230).
invariants: Permission precedence is deny > ask > allow and never depends on hook registration order.
A hook infrastructure failure is a non-blocking outcome (no exit code), while a hook that DOES answer deny/ask is honored as a gate.
Hook runs inherit the agent's session workspace as cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and a hookSpecificOutput block naming a different event is discarded.

mechanisms.name: client-approval-and-permission-surfaces
mechanisms.what: The browser half answers the host approval waterfall and drives permission switches, both over the Remote plane rather than a slash-command surface. ui-approval subscribes with ctx.remote.$on('approval/request'), wraps the request in a PendingApproval with a one-shot render key, registers it as a pending interaction and renders it as a conversation.composer takeover whose only outcomes are 'allowed-once' and 'rejected' (packages/client/ui-approval/src/client/index.ts:35-68, 90-92; ApprovalPanel.tsx:26-29); an unanswered request delegates to the next waterfall listener, and a signal abort settles it so a late answer is discarded (contract/slots.ts:122-159). ui-permission-presets decorates the host /permission command as a popupSelect reading the session's 'permissions' projection, marks the current value, filters the derived 'custom' state out of the pick targets, and attaches an explicit confirmation gate to the FULL_ACCESS_PRESET 'danger-full-access' row; a pick submits '/permission <preset>' so the host command remains the single write path (ui-permission-presets/src/client/index.ts:59-79, 145-166; presentation.ts:4). Its General-settings row separately writes the default preset for sessions created later through the host Settings API (index.ts:125-143).
invariants: Only one-shot decisions cross the client boundary: the UI cannot express 'always allow'.
The picker exists exactly while the host projection does; otherwise the bare invocation falls through to the host command.
The Full access preset always carries an explicit risk confirmation before the switch is submitted.

mechanisms.name: human-question-tool-seam
mechanisms.what: The ask_user_question tool is a model-facing Consumer of ctx.userQuestions: it registers a tool whose required input is an array of {id, question, header?, options?, multi_select?} and whose output is {answers:[{id, selected[], custom?}]}, mapping the wire naming (multi_select -> multiSelect) in execute (packages/interaction/tool-ask-user/src/index.ts:19-100). It passes the calling agent and the tool-execution signal into ctx.userQuestions.ask and feeds the human answer back as an ordinary tool result, so the loop pauses while a UI provider answers (80-99). The underlying seam is fail-closed: an aborted signal throws UserQuestionError ASK_ABORTED, an empty question list is refused, and a supplied agent that is not the registry's exact live runtime root throws CALLER_NOT_LIVE / DELEGATED_CALLER so an owned child with no human answerer cannot block forever (packages/interaction/user-questions/src/index.ts:41-47, 70-90).
invariants: The tool never fabricates an answer: the result is the provider's answer or a structured error.
Human interaction is valid only for the exact live runtime root, not for durable session lineage.

mechanisms.name: advisory-repeat-tool-guard
mechanisms.what: repeat-tool-reminder is an advisory per-agent repeat-call detector, not a gate: it observes on tools/post-execute, counts consecutive identical calls per agent in a WeakMap keyed by JSON.stringify([toolName, canonicalizedArguments]) where canonicalization deep-sorts JSON keys, and at each configured threshold injects a user-role reminder sourced as a plugin notice (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:189-207). It always delegates with next() and folds its reminder onto whatever the downstream decision was — a blocked call still gets the nudge — so it never vetoes or rewrites a call (209-224), and an agent/pre-step carrying a user message deletes the chain because repetition across an interjection is not a loop (226-232). Config is fail-loud at load: thresholds must be non-empty, integers >= 2, duplicate-free (normalized ascending, with thresholds[0] the gentle tier), and argumentsPreviewChars must be an integer >= 1 (128-141, 169-171). Only the model-visible preview is truncated; the chain key always compares the full canonical string (118-121).
invariants: Observe-and-enrich, never veto: counting happens first (state advances regardless of the downstream outcome), then the guard delegates and only prepends context.
Untracked calls (include/exclude wildcards) are transparent: they neither count nor reset.
A denied call still counts, because ToolRuntime routes denials through the same post-execute pipeline.

mechanisms.name: preset-scope-isolation-gate
mechanisms.what: mountPreset is the gate that keeps a per-agent preset composition from changing process-global behaviour: it refuses to mount into an unscoped context because 'its registrations would apply to every agent in the process' (packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts:378-385), then, after await() settles, it fails the mount if any row did not activate (403-406) and rejects any row that published a process-global service, telling the author to put it behind an `isolate` realm or move it to the host composition (407-413). The subtree is owned by the agent's fiber so it unwinds with the agent and a rejection leaves nothing mounted (369-376, 415-424). This is the constraint that stops a preset row from re-registering host-global capabilities such as the sandbox provider, filesystem or approval service for the whole process.
invariants: A preset mounts only into a scoped agent context; an unscoped mount is refused before anything is created.
A row that publishes a process-global service fails the whole mount instead of leaking into the host realm.
A rejected mount disposes its subtree, so failure is not partially applied.

moduleCoverage.shell/pwsh-sandbox: shell-confinement-wrap-and-denial-classification (deliberate call-for-call mirror of the bash executor)
moduleCoverage.preset/persona: none - this row only registers systemPrompt persona prefix/suffix sections (and optionally suppresses the runtime-context snapshot) at packages/preset/persona/src/index.ts:62-74; it carries no permission, sandbox, approval or gating logic.
moduleCoverage.identity/anonymous-user-id: none in this domain - contributes the model-domain mechanism `deepseek-wire-protocol-and-request-extensions` by supplying the per-harness-home random UUID that the DeepSeek adapter sends as the x-deepseek-harness-user-id header (packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:544); it holds no confinement or approval logic.
moduleCoverage.client/ui-approval: client-approval-and-permission-surfaces; approval-service-policy-and-audit-pair (the browser answerer of its approval/request waterfall)
moduleCoverage.client/ui-permission-presets: client-approval-and-permission-surfaces; permission-preset-bundling-and-knob-write-path (its settings row writes the default preset for future sessions)

mechanisms.name: llm-adapter-registry-and-route-resolution
mechanisms.what: LlmRuntime (ctx.llm) is an adapter registry keyed by provider route: registerAdapter(providers, adapter) is all-or-nothing (empty set, duplicate route or bad providerInfo throws INVALID_ADAPTER/DUPLICATE_ADAPTER) and publishes llm/adapters-updated with each listener contained so one broken observer cannot veto the commit, while INVARIANT-coded failures still surface (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:345-371, 387-445). Routes can be atomically replaced in one synchronous section through the returned handle, so no request observes a gap between release and re-registration, and a disposed handle throws REGISTRATION_DISPOSED (454-462, 407-415). Dormant routes an adapter could activate through configuration live in a separate directory (registerConfigurableProviders, INVALID_DIRECTORY/DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY, listConfigurableProviders @Remote) so configuration surfaces can show live and dormant providers together (481-543). Dispatch resolves strictly through registration(), which throws NO_ADAPTER for an unregistered route (964-968).
invariants: One route maps to exactly one adapter registration; a candidate route set is validated in full before anything is mutated.
Registry notifications are non-vetoing but never silently swallowed; INVARIANT failures rethrow after every listener ran.
An unregistered provider is a hard NO_ADAPTER failure, never a silent fallback.
constants: error codes on this seam: INVALID_ADAPTER, DUPLICATE_ADAPTER, REGISTRATION_DISPOSED, INVALID_DIRECTORY, DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY, NO_ADAPTER (index.ts:395-429, 496-529, 966)

mechanisms.name: model-catalogue-and-exact-model-metadata
mechanisms.what: Model knowledge has two clearly separated levels. The advisory catalogue (LlmAdapter.listModels) is validated and deduplicated by LlmRuntime (INVALID_CATALOG) but explicitly never controls routing or rejects a request (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:232-241, 691-718). Exact metadata for one route comes from resolveModel/prepareCall and is normalized by normalizeModelInfo: identity must match provider and model, context.contextWindow must be a positive integer (INVALID_MODEL_CONTEXT), defaultMaxTokens must be a positive safe integer (INVALID_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS), systemPromptUpdate must be 'in-history', and a reasoning block must carry at least one effort, unique non-empty ids, and a defaultEffort that names a declared effort (INVALID_MODEL_REASONING) (747-846). Adapters own the concrete catalogues: DeepSeek ships DEFAULT_MODELS (deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp) with contextWindow/inputModalities/image budgets/systemPromptUpdate and validates every entry (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:92-122, 224-269), while pi-ai materializes each model as installed-catalog entry spread overridden by the profile, with contextWindow = entry ?? base ?? request.defaultContextWindow and maxTokens = entry ?? base ?? request.defaultMaxTokens (llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts:901-930).
invariants: Catalogue membership is advisory; an adapter may accept unlisted model ids and absence must never become request rejection.
Exact-model metadata is validated at the seam boundary, so a misbehaving adapter fails loud instead of poisoning downstream pricing/preflight decisions.
pi-ai keeps the model's capability maxTokens separate from the deployment's defaultMaxTokens, because they answer different questions (catalog.ts:809-811).
constants: DeepSeek catalog entries: 4 default models; per-entry contextWindow, maxTokens, inputModalities min 1, imagePixelBudget ('low' or positive integer), imageMaxBytes (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:92-122, 175-185)
validation codes: INVALID_CATALOG, INVALID_MODEL_INFO, INVALID_MODEL_CONTEXT, INVALID_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS, INVALID_MODEL_REASONING (llm/llm/src/index.ts:706, 762-838)

mechanisms.name: provider-model-discovery-service
mechanisms.what: Discovery is keyed by settings namespace rather than by route, because a provider being ADDED has no route to name: registerModelDiscovery(settingsNs, discover) registers an offer that is disposed with the fiber, and discoverModels(settingsNs, request, signal) requires either a provider route or a baseURL (INVALID_DISCOVERY), throws NO_DISCOVERY for an unregistered namespace, and deduplicates by id in endpoint order (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:555-617). The same operation is exposed on the RPC plane as @Remote('discoverModels') remoteDiscoverModels, wrapping any failure in RemoteError 'llm/model-discovery-rejected' carrying the settings namespace and endpoint (627-646, declared at types.ts:274-282). The pi-ai adapter answers a route its installed catalogue ships from that catalogue with no network call, and only interrogates routes it does not describe over LISTABLE_PROTOCOLS (anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses); responses are capped at MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (llm-pi-ai/src/discovery.ts:1-43, 48-58).
invariants: Discovery is a draft interrogation: nothing is stored, and settings.yaml remains the only thing that decides what a route serves.
A namespace is the addressing key, so a provider being added can be interrogated before it has a route.
A protocol whose listing shape is unknown reports that it cannot be interrogated rather than guessing response fields (Azure, Codex/OAuth and the remaining pi-ai protocols are deliberately absent).

mechanisms.name: reasoning-effort-translation
mechanisms.what: Harness-side reasoning effort is an opaque adapter-owned ReasoningEffortId. The seam validates it against the exact model's declared efforts and materializes the adapter's defaultEffort into the request config; an explicit unsupported effort throws UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT before any provider I/O, with no clamping or aliasing, and the materialized fields are recorded on the prepared call as adapterDefaults so logging can distinguish caller choice from adapter default (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:872-906, 925-932; call-config.ts:23-39). The DeepSeek adapter translates the resolved effort into its wire pair: 'off' -> thinking disabled (never sent as a wire effort), 'low'|'high'|'max' -> thinking enabled plus reasoning_effort, and a session-title purpose forces thinking disabled; a deployment with thinking:'disabled' rejects any non-off effort both at load and at request time (llm-deepseek/src/serialize.ts:71-99, 362-364; index.ts:311-315). Its resolved model metadata advertises either the off-only effort list or the four-level list with the configured default (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:168-200, 418-436).
invariants: The effort vocabulary is adapter-owned and opaque to the harness; the seam only checks membership in the declared set.
Unsupported explicit efforts reject before provider I/O; no silent clamping, aliasing or dropping.
'off' is a harness/thinking concept and must never be emitted as a provider wire effort.
constants: DeepSeek efforts: off, low, high, max; default when unset: high (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:168-200; llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:132, 141-142)

mechanisms.name: context-window-and-max-output-metadata
mechanisms.what: Context capacity and the output cap are resolved per exact route and materialized into the call: resolveCallWithInfo fills maxTokens from the adapter's defaultMaxTokens only when the caller omitted one, and returns the LlmModelContext alongside the config (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:872-905). prepareCall then detaches and deep-freezes the config, the context and the modalities, and records which of reasoningEffort/maxTokens the adapter supplied rather than the caller (921-942); LlmAdapter.prepareCall binds that metadata to the same adapter generation as the eventual dispatch, so a settings change between preparation and dispatch cannot combine one generation's capabilities with another's endpoint (259-274). The DeepSeek adapter defaults are DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 1,000,000 and DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 256,000 with per-model overrides, and an uncatalogued model is advertised as text-only rather than claiming unverified image capability (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:145-149, 400-417).
invariants: An adapter-supplied default is materialized only when the caller omitted the field; adapterDefaults records the difference for logging.
Capability metadata is captured with the dispatch generation, so preparation and dispatch never mix generations.
Unverified capability is not advertised: an unknown model is reported text-only.
constants: deepseek config bounds: fileExpiresAfterSeconds 3_600..2_592_000 (default 604_800); fileQuotaCleanupBatch 1..1_000 (default 100); filesApiTimeoutMs default 60_000; maxInlineRequestImageBytes default 20 MiB; imageOffloadByteQuantum default 64 MiB; inlineImageOffloadByteQuantum default 10 MiB; imageOffloadCountQuantum default 20; maxImagesPerRequest default 600 (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:152-166, 195-205)

mechanisms.name: provider-credential-resolution-and-layered-sources
mechanisms.what: The credential seam has two key spaces: a CredentialRef (an environment-variable-shaped name) answers what is behind that name through layered resolution, and a CredentialKey ('<scope>/<id>') answers what credential a plugin holds for one of its own ids, where presence of the record is the whole fact and modifyRecord is the only write path because a correct write depends on the current value (packages/credentials/credentials/src/index.ts:19-22, 154-250). Resolution is per operation and must not be cached, an empty stored value is absent everywhere, and set/unset reject while a read-only source shadows the reference (175-209). The local provider lays the sources in trust order — inherited process environment (read-only, wins) > $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml (managed, writable) > cwd/.env > $DSH_HOME/.env — and reports the winning layer as the source id 'env' | 'file' | <dotenv> (credentials-local/src/index.ts:1-27, 617-639). Adapters then enforce the transport invariant: normalizeApiKey trims and accepts only printable ASCII excluding space, and assertUsableApiKey throws INVALID_CREDENTIAL without ever echoing the key (llm/llm/src/api-key.ts:15, 36-41; llm/llm/src/index.ts:145-160). DeepSeek re-resolves the key per request and sends it as 'authorization: Bearer' (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:479, 539-541); pi-ai refuses to fall back to ambient discovery once a profile names a credential reference, throwing MISSING_CREDENTIAL instead of silently billing another tenant (llm-pi-ai/src/index.ts:168-191).
invariants: Secrets never round-trip to a surface: describe/describeRecord/listRecords expose presence, kind and writability, never the value.
Consumers re-resolve per operation and must not cache across operations, which is what makes a changed credential reach the next request without a restart.
A named credential reference that does not resolve is a hard MISSING_CREDENTIAL, never a fallback to ambient discovery.
constants: credentials document path: $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; file mode 0o600, dir mode 0o700; group/other bits 0o077 rejected; document version 1 (credentials-local/src/index.ts:61, 97, 167, 699)

mechanisms.name: oauth-authorization-flow-registry
mechanisms.what: ctx.authorization owns the human conversation and lifecycle of obtaining a credential, never the protocol: a plugin registers an AuthorizationFlow keyed by the CredentialKey it writes, with a label and a non-empty methods tuple, and the flow talks to whichever surface started it through one neutral vocabulary of notify/prompt (packages/credentials/authorization/src/index.ts:1-27, 90-159). Registration is one flow per key (DUPLICATE_FLOW) and a flow leaving mid-attempt aborts its running attempt, because the fiber that could answer for it is going away (202-218). begin() enforces one attempt per key at a time (ALREADY_IN_FLIGHT), refuses an unknown method (UNKNOWN_METHOD) and an unclaimed key (NO_FLOW), returns 'cancelled' for a signal already aborted before the slot is claimed, and only reports 'authorized' when the flow's record was committed and observed during the attempt (NOT_COMMITTED otherwise); the key slot is released before authorization/settled is fanned out with contained listeners (258-347). The write itself goes through ctx.credentials.modifyRecord, which the seam requires (static inject = ['credentials'], line 184); pi-ai stores its OAuth grant payload verbatim as an opaque grant record so the library keeps owning its token format (llm-pi-ai/src/auth.ts:64-100).
invariants: The seam owns the lifecycle and never the protocol: a second authorization protocol arrives as another flow, not another seam.
One attempt per key at a time; a second caller is refused rather than joined, because it would prompt a different human through the same flow.
Success requires an observed credential-record commit; a flow that resolves without writing is NOT_COMMITTED.
constants: error codes: DUPLICATE_FLOW, NO_FLOW, UNKNOWN_METHOD, ALREADY_IN_FLIGHT, NOT_COMMITTED (authorization/src/index.ts:206, 279-288, 272)
declined prompt code: 'DECLINED' via AuthorizationDeclinedError, settling the attempt as cancelled (authorization/src/index.ts:79-84)

mechanisms.name: provider-retry-policy-and-execution
mechanisms.what: Retry policy is provider-owned and resolved once when the route is registered: resolveRetryPolicy validates and freezes either a bounded 'normal' policy (mode, maxRetries, retryableCodes, backoff) or an unbounded 'always' policy, rejecting unknown keys, a non-positive or over-large delay, initialDelayMs > maxDelayMs, and an out-of-range jitter ratio (packages/llm/llm/src/retry-policy.ts:26-103, 121-194); prepareRoutes captures the resolved policy on the AdapterRegistration (llm/llm/src/index.ts:436-442) and providerRetryPolicy(provider) reads it back (653-655). Execution lives in the optional dsh-llm-retry plugin on the agent's request-recovery waterfall: a 'normal' policy only handles its configured retryable codes, an 'always' policy retries every failure until success, cancellation or disposal; the attempt is made durable as an llm/retry event BEFORE the cancellable wait and llm/retry-started after it, with the retry counter folded from the llmRetry session projection keyed by provider plus a policy key (llm-retry/src/index.ts:194-241, 123-138). A provider-supplied providerRetryAfterMs is honored only when it does not exceed maxDelayMs under a normal policy (otherwise the decision passes downstream); otherwise the delay is exponential with symmetric jitter clamped to maxDelayMs (227-240, 59-64).
invariants: The policy is immutable registration state: a change re-registers the route rather than mutating a live policy.
Every scheduled retry is durable in the session log before its cancellable wait, and a disposal aborts and drains active recovery.
The harness never retries INVALID_CREDENTIAL by default, because a malformed credential fails identically on every attempt.
constants: default retryable codes: EMPTY_RESPONSE, RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT (retry-policy.ts:18-24)
delays bounded by MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS from dsh-timeout (retry-policy.ts:82-83)

mechanisms.name: streaming-call-dispatch-and-chunk-assembly
mechanisms.what: LlmRuntime.stream routes every call through the ctx.waterfall('llm/stream') chain into adapterStream, which resolves the registration, normalizes exact-model metadata, materializes the call config, projects file attachments to text handles (files are never dispatched natively) and strips images for models whose inputModalities exclude 'image' (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:1011-1058, 1106-1120). Adapter selection, dispatch, iterator construction and iteration failures all become one terminal finish chunk — {kind:'aborted'} when the signal aborted, else {kind:'error'} — while middleware, nested-call, cleanup and consumer failures stay thrown (1060-1093, 1124-1132). The consumer half is BlockAssembler, the single canonical chunk-to-message algorithm: it tolerates delta-only protocols, ignores deltas and re-closes arriving after a block was closed, drops tool-call blocks under a max-tokens finish because they cannot be executed safely, and prunes the adapter's replay envelope in step with the emitted blocks (discarding it entirely when entries do not align) (assembler.ts:38-96, 130-150). It also exposes interruptedBlocks() — closed and open text/reasoning blocks with non-whitespace content, tool calls omitted — as the prefix a cancelled stream can safely finalize (169-179).
invariants: Every adapter-side failure becomes a terminal chunk in the stream protocol; only middleware and consumer failures throw.
One keep/drop decision governs both emitted blocks and replay metadata, so stored content and stored metadata cannot disagree.
An interrupted stream finalizes text/reasoning only: a retained tool call would require a fabricated result.
constants: finish reason defaults to {kind:'stop'} when no finish chunk arrived (assembler.ts:186-189)

mechanisms.name: llm-failure-taxonomy-and-normalization
mechanisms.what: Failures are classified by a stable machine-routable code on HarnessError, explicitly never by parsing the message (packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts:13-22). The seam publishes canonical provider-neutral codes — CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED, QUOTA, EMPTY_RESPONSE (a degenerate completion carrying no content blocks, classified as a failure instead of yielding an empty assistant message, and safe to retry) and INVALID_CREDENTIAL (malformed rather than absent, deliberately outside the default retryable set) — plus regex classifiers that recognize the context-overflow wording used by OpenAI-compatible providers (error.ts:24-80). normalizeLlmFailure is the adapter-boundary chokepoint: it detaches serializable provider facts, trusts an error's carried `failure` payload only when its own `code` data property agrees after validation, reads via own-property descriptors so SDK-defined accessors cannot run, tolerates non-Error throws, and maps third-party SDK codes to 'UNKNOWN' because they are not this taxonomy (adapter-failure.ts:16-28, 40-104).
invariants: Consumers route on `code`, never on message text.
Foreign SDK codes are not adopted into the taxonomy; only Harness-owned codes survive normalization.
A degenerate empty completion is a classified failure, not an empty assistant message.
constants: status validation range 100..599 on a carried failure snapshot (adapter-failure.ts:74)

mechanisms.name: deepseek-wire-protocol-and-request-extensions
mechanisms.what: The DeepSeek adapter speaks chat-completions over SSE: it serializes thinking/reasoning_effort and messages into the wire body (llm-deepseek/src/serialize.ts:82-99, 360-364) and sends 'authorization: Bearer <key>', 'accept: text/event-stream', the mandatory attribution headers, 'x-deepseek-harness-user-id' (the anonymous harness-home id) and 'x-deepseek-harness-session-id', plus 'x-deepseek-harness-compact: 1' for a compaction-purpose request (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:539-551). A per-read idle watchdog enforces streamIdleTimeoutMs and reports LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT, while caller aborts map to ABORTED and anything else to TRANSPORT (adapter.ts:481-527, 166-167). Attribution is centralized so adapters cannot drift and cannot suppress it: attributionHeaders() defaults to APP_IDENTITY {product:'deepseek-harness', version from package.json, repository url} rendered as 'product/version (+url)' (llm/llm/src/attribution.ts:40-67), a contract stated on LlmAdapter itself (llm/llm/src/index.ts:194-199). Independent top-level request fields are owned by plugins through the deepseek-llm-api-extensions registry: register() claims one field name exclusively and prepare() runs every provider from one immutable base request, freezing cloned values and returning a joint, idempotent accept() transaction that settles every callback before reporting failures (deepseek-llm-api-extensions/src/index.ts:79-129).
invariants: Every provider HTTP request must carry the attribution headers; nothing can suppress them.
One plugin owns one top-level request field; a second registration of the same field throws.
Extension preparation failures reject before HTTP dispatch, and callers hold no mutable alias to the outgoing request.
constants: default endpoint: https://api.deepseek.com, overridable by $DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL from a trusted environment layer (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:209-213, 394-396)
provider route: 'deepseek-official'; default credential ref: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:88-90)

mechanisms.name: plugin-package-attribution-inventory
mechanisms.what: plugin-package-inventory-deepseek contributes a 'dsh_plugin_packages' top-level field to official DeepSeek requests through the extension registry: prepare() collects the active Loader entries (excluding groups, disabled rows and non-ACTIVE fibers), optionally adds the requesting agent's standing preset tree resolved through agentPresets/standingMountFor, and resolves each entry's owning package manifest {name, version} either by bare-package search anchored on the tree base or by walking up from the module path to the nearest package.json (packages/llm/plugin-package-inventory-deepseek/src/index.ts:131-179, 186-198). Installed dependencies that no active row loads, and loose modules with no package manifest, are excluded; the payload is version 1 and the list is sorted deterministically without relying on host locale or ICU data (145-178, 192-197).
invariants: Only ACTIVE, non-structural Loader entries count as loaded plugins; an installed-but-unused dependency is not reported.
The order is deterministic independent of host locale, so the same plugin set always serializes identically.
A package entry that cannot be resolved throws rather than silently dropping from the inventory.

mechanisms.name: token-metering-and-usage-projection
mechanisms.what: TokenMeter is a replay-aware service over the durable session log: it folds a per-session surface and registers the tokenUsage, contextPressure and contextBreakdown projection units (packages/llm/token-meter/src/index.ts:100-122). measure() reuses provider usage only when the latest successful call's canonical request envelope matches the one being measured and the provider total is no lower than that call's full route-priced anchor; otherwise the whole envelope and surface are repriced, so a provider that under-reports cannot mask growth (145-150, 46-67). Provider usage is summed from disjoint buckets — inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens + outputTokens — so reasoning output is never double-counted (69-75). Surface pricing asks the routed adapter for image pricing (LlmAdapter.imageRequestPricing, resolved per measurement, synchronous, no I/O) and fails loud if the number of prices does not match the number of image occurrences, because misalignment would silently misprice nodes (route-pricing.ts:23-76; llm/llm/src/index.ts:219-230, 666-668).
invariants: Provider usage is trusted only under a matching canonical envelope and a total no lower than the route-priced anchor.
Pricing answers must align one-to-one with the priced occurrences; a mismatch throws rather than mispricing.
The meter accepts no configuration keys at all: validateConfigKeys throws on any key.
constants: no supported config keys; any key throws (index.ts:86-91, 103)
usage buckets summed: inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens + outputTokens (index.ts:70-75)

mechanisms.name: agent-default-model-resolution
mechanisms.what: AgentDefaultModelConfig (ctx.agentDefaultModel) owns the default model selection for Agents created without an explicit one, independently of any Host or transport: a composition entry {provider, model} is always usable on its own, and when a settings provider is mounted the 'agent-default-model' section supplies a live user layer read through currentSelection() (packages/core/agent-default-model/src/index.ts:20-38, 64-92). The projection onto the Agent-facing ModelSelection converts the stored reasoningEffort string into a branded ReasoningEffortId, and saveSelection writes the complete selection back through ctx.settings.replace, tolerating a deployment with no settings provider (48-57, 94-106). Because every consumer reads through currentSelection(), no registration-level fact needs rebuilding when the settings document changes (76-82).
invariants: The composition entry is always usable without a settings provider; the user layer is optional and read live.
The stored selection is projected into a branded ModelSelection at the boundary, so an unvalidated string never reaches request headers.
Save writes the complete selection (provider, model and optional reasoning effort) so a partial update cannot leave a stale effort behind.

mechanisms.name: http-proxy-transport-policy
mechanisms.what: Node's fetch ignores HTTP_PROXY, so this library resolves one process-wide policy from the launch environment and installs it as undici's global dispatcher, which is what fetch resolves — covering LLM adapters, web search, MCP over HTTP and telemetry without touching their code (packages/util/http-proxy/src/index.ts:1-23; install.ts:194-215). Policy resolution is pure and transport-free: it reads each name lowercase-first with the uppercase fallback and treats a blank value as unset (undici's own ?? chain would let an empty lowercase name shadow a populated uppercase one), merges LOOPBACK_NO_PROXY unconditionally because a proxying harness would route its own Web UI and local servers into a loop, routes only http:/https: URLs, and reports SOCKS/PAC values as diagnostics instead of silently dropping them (policy.ts:33-98, 109-118). A rejected slot is distinct from an absent one, so a scheme whose proxy was rejected stays direct rather than borrowing another scheme's proxy. The install publishes the resolved policy into the proxy environment variables for consumers that read the environment and for spawned children, and exposes clearedProxyEnv() as the overlay that strips every proxy name from a replay child (install.ts:70-92, 228-254, 296-314).
invariants: The loopback bypass is not optional and is always merged into the policy.
A value this package cannot route is reported, never silently dropped, and never replaced by another scheme's proxy.
The policy is plain data with no methods, so worker threads receive the identical policy through structured clone rather than re-reading a possibly different environment.
constants: routed schemes: http:, https:; SOCKS/PAC schemes only named in a diagnostic (policy.ts:57-60)
env names per field: http_proxy/HTTP_PROXY, https_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY, no_proxy/NO_PROXY, plus the all_proxy/ALL_PROXY fallback that is resolved but never written back (policy.ts:39-54)

notes: Scope: source-only audit of D:\agent-complete\deepseek-harness-dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 at v0.1.5-rc.2 (read-only; nothing in that tree was modified). Every evidence line above was opened with the read tool in this session; `verified` is true for all 31 mechanisms (16 safety, 15 model). Paths are relative to the source root.  method: Files were located by directory walk over packages/, then read directly (src/ only, never README or docs). Line ranges cited are exactly the ranges returned by the read tool; where a citation is a doc comment inside src/ it is labelled as such in the `what` text where that matters.  cordisPlumbing: Several modules in the requested list are Cordis plumbing or seams with no safety/model policy of their own and are called out as such in moduleCoverage: preset/agent-presets is a generic per-agent composition loader (its only gate is preset-scope-isolation-gate), preset/persona only registers systemPrompt sections (contributes no mechanism), interaction/tool-ask-user is a thin model-facing consumer of ctx.userQuestions (human-question-tool-seam), and util/http-proxy is an explicit non-plugin library. The service seams themselves (sandbox/sandbox, sandbox/sandbox-policy, interaction/user-approval, credentials/credentials, credentials/authorization, llm/llm) are Service Definition packages with real mechanism content, not plumbing.  rpcVsCommands: Command surface is not slash-centric. The permission switch does have a /permission command (registered by interaction/permission-presets and decorated by client/ui-permission-presets as a popupSelect), but everything else in these two domains is exposed on seams and the Typert @Remote RPC plane: llm.listProviders (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:468), llm.listConfigurableProviders (line 540) and Remote('discoverModels') remoteDiscoverModels (line 627, error code 'llm/model-discovery-rejected'); agent-presets discovery/authoring is reached through RemoteError codes ('agent-preset/invalid', 'gateway/bad-request') in preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts and authoring.ts; approval and permission state travel as session projections ('approval/asked'+'approval/decided' events, 'permissions' projection stateVersion 2, 'sandboxMode' stateVersion 1) consumed by clients over the Remote Event waterfall (ctx.remote.$on('approval/request')). No capability was treated as absent merely because it has no slash command.  readVsWriteIsolation: Read vs write is asymmetric by design and each backend states its own boundary: fs-sandbox fences ONLY the two mutations and lets reads pass because every mode permits reading; Landlock grants readOnly ['/'] with a readWrite list; bwrap ro-binds / and only adds a writable bind under workspace-write; Seatbelt emits '(deny file-write*)' with narrow allows; windows-acl restricts WRITE only and explicitly documents that reads, network and process visibility are not restricted. No read-side confinement mechanism exists in these packages.  dangerClassification: There is no separately named 'danger classification' service. Danger is expressed as (a) the closed SandboxMode union where danger-full-access means the fs sandbox 'does not restrict file modifications' (renderPolicyContext, packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:41-55), (b) the strictly-wider escalation table in packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts, and (c) the client-side explicit risk gate on the 'danger-full-access' preset (packages/client/ui-permission-presets/src/client/presentation.ts:4 plus the confirmation block in that package's client/index.ts:67-77).  unverifiedOrPartial: No claim in this file is uncited, but three evidence sets are partial reads rather than whole-file reads: packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts (lines 130-1147 read; 1-129 not), packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts (190-429), packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts (1-90, 90-269, 300-429 of 514), packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts (160-279, 375-454, 460-579 of 715), packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts (888-932 of 957), packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/discovery.ts (1-120 of 362), packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/auth.ts (1-110 of 231), packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/index.ts (60-199 of 337), packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts (1-130, 600-659 of 935), packages/credentials/authorization/src/index.ts (1-349 of 437), packages/util/http-proxy/src/policy.ts (1-140 of 343), packages/util/http-proxy/src/install.ts (1-120, 185-254, 290-314 of 315), packages/llm/token-meter/src/index.ts (1-150 of 328), packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts (365-424 of 433), packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/index.ts (1-90 of 190), packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts (220-239 of 327), packages/interaction/user-questions/src/index.ts (1-90 of 154). Each cited line lies inside a range actually read. two client-side mechanisms are described from their client entry points only: neither packages/client/ui-approval nor packages/client/ui-permission-presets was traced into the shared slot/popup shells it renders through (those live in other client packages outside this module list). windows-acl confinement is documented by its own module as partial enforcement (Everyone stays in the restricting list; NTFS hard links alias one file object), and the code reports that honestly as STATIC_ENFORCEMENT['windows-acl'] = 'partial' rather than claiming full coverage. hooks-as-permission-gates records two capabilities the code itself marks incomplete: merged.stop (continue:false) is logged but has no run-level halt (TODO(hook-continue-false) at packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:188), and Claude hook updatedInput/systemMessage are logged and warned but not honored (lines 174-179). Codex additionally honors deny only, not allow/ask (packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts:223-230). preset/agent-presets is mounted through a Loader entry tree whose per-preset composition files were not enumerated in this pass; the isolation gate above is the part of that package that bears on confinement, and its roster/discovery half contributes no safety mechanism.
